text:
Alex K: throwing this on the channel — found a reproducible window where reads after a prefix handoff return older KV values for ~100-300ms. repro harness attached to ticket. logs show owner_epoch bumped but cache still serving older blob.

Maria D: thanks. is this the same symptom as the earlier stale-read incident? any correlation with prefill timing?

Alex K: similar but narrower: when handoff completes we publish ownership early to route traffic; cache warmup and last_applied propagation are async. if a reader hits before warmup, they get stale.

Samir R: three mitigations I can think of: 1) read-side epoch guard: consult in-memory owner_epoch map and reject serve if cached_epoch < owner_epoch; 2) push synchronous invalidation to all subscribers at handoff; 3) bump handoff to be atomic (advertise only after local snapshot applied).

Lee P: 1 is quick but adds a memory lookup on the hot path — should be O(1) and RCU-protected. 2 is best-effort pubsub; lost messages mean fallback needed. 3 is safest but touches control plane and could increase latency for handoffs.

Nora T: ops note: if we aggressively invalidate/purge, we'll flood rehydrate traffic and spike GPU load. need a cooldown/backoff and telemetry to detect chase storms.

Maria D: proposal: short-term combo: add read-side epoch check + best-effort invalidation messages at handoff + a configurable cooldown window that suppresses invalidations for cold prefixes. gate behind feature flag.

Samir R: implement read-epoch-check as: if cached_entry.epoch < owner_map.get(prefix,0) then trigger a direct store read (sync) and optionally update cache. add metric evict.epoch_mismatch_count and histogram for added latency.

Lee P: invalidation message should carry prefix, new_epoch, last_write_ts, and an idempotency nonce. subscribers can decide to drop or prefetch. also include a hint: "recreate_preload=true/false" to avoid thundering-herd for large prefixes.

Nora T: add server-side rate limit: if invalidations/sec > 5*k nodes, switch to lazy mode for that prefix and emit alert. ops will add a Grafana panel for invalidation rate, rehydrate QPS, and stale_reads.

Alex K: long-term: handshake refactor where ownership isn't announced until local KV snapshot and last_applied are persisted and visible. requires changes to handoff protocol but gives atomicity. we should RFC that separately.

Maria D: rollout plan: Samir builds PR for epoch-check + flags + metrics. Lee wires invalidation publisher in handoff flow. Nora prepares dashboards and an automated canary job. Gate: land in feature-flagged form, enable on a small canary cohort for 72h, monitor stale_reads and rehydrate QPS.

Samir R: taking the read-path work and tests. will include unit tests simulating lost invalidation and epoch mismatch. will add a cache-entry version byte to allow schema evolution.

Lee P: infra pieces: implementing invalidation pubsub and backoff knob. will include a kill-switch config and an env var to toggle aggressive invalidation.

Nora T: ops actions: dashboard, alert rule when evict.epoch_mismatch_count > 50/min on canary, and automated rollback if rehydrate QPS > baseline*3.

Alex K: action items recap: Samir -> PR + tests + metrics, Lee -> invalidation pubsub + knobs, Nora -> dashboards + canary job, Maria -> customer-impact scan to find tenants that observed stale reads recently, Alex -> draft RFC for handshake atomicity. target: land short-term bits this sprint (5bd).

prefill-bot: NOTICE: canary subscription for invalidation created on 4 nodes. debug channel: #prefill-debug.

Alex K: thanks everyone. ping me if canary shows odd regressions. we'll decide on atomic handshake after data from the canary.
